title: Back in New York 1943-51: Dixieland with Art Hodes, Red Allen fill-ins
summary: Returning in 1943-44 he gigged around New York saving to return to France, worked as a Dixieland trumpeter with Art Hodes and subbed for Red Allen, while bebop was emerging.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So, that was the end of that scene in Canada. Now, when I come back again, I'm coming back in '43 and '44, I start giggin all around again. Just kept on gigging and gigging.
Because I was amassing a bankroll to go back to France at the end of the war. So, in 1951, I had about --
Oh, so you stayed around New York until 1951?
Yeah, I stayed around New York until 1951 and reamassed myself.
Then, in '51, February 8th, I went to Patterson....
Now, were you working as a leader when you were working around New York in the '40's or were you --
Sometimes I was a leader and sometimes I -- now, now, now, I started working with Art Hodes/ I started working with Dixieland bands. Mostly with Art Hodes. I was a Dixieland man then.
And, and, and, Red Allen, I filled in for Red Allen on most of his jobs. So, I went to Paris --
At that time too, be-bop was emerging wasn't it?
Oh, yes, be-bop was -- Thelonious Monk and Joe Guy and what's that drummer?
Kenny Clarke, they was down losing their minds down there, and Teddy Hill was running it
